threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their hesitation at the bus stop, like they're waiting for a tube that doesn't exist here.
Last night on the 3, saw a guy arguing with a lamppost like it owed him money. Brixton can be wild when the sun goes down.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid bouncing a soccer ball on the sidewalk while their grandma knitted on the balcony. That blend of old and new feels just right.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it’s common to see people chilling on the sidewalk at 2 a.m. with their beer, just casually chatting. Feels like a slice of life you won't find elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they avoid the BART at Civic Center without blinking, thanks to the train's random smoke outbursts lately.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Sitting on the 21, a guy serenades us with an off-key version of ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ while the bus screeches to a halt. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think they need to visit Park Güell, but real Gràcians know the hidden gems are the little plazas with local festas during summer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered face while ordering at a local bakery, still trying to figure out the 'pan' vs 'barra' distinction.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it 'The Overground,' not just a train to Hackney. You still think it’s a fashionable area instead of just home.
Caught a glimpse of a lad singing to his thumb guitar- didn't know you could strum 'Wonderwall' in a bus seat. Everyone just nodded along.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a quiet café on a side street with the best homemade vegan cake, I knew Neukölln had become my home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find an art installation in an old toilet building, showcasing local artists while serving as a quirky gallery.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they snag a burrito during a BART delay without missing a beat, while newcomers just stare at the chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo napping on the 14 today, clutching a bouquet. Guess even weddings can turn into Muni adventures.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think we spend all day in cafes. But locals know the real charm is in the late-night chats on the street—with just the right light from the lampposts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still fumble with the metro map, asking for directions in English as if it’s a tourist attraction.
